Declared independent on a man-made platform in the Adriatic in 1968, this micronation used Esperanto as its official language before being demolished by Italian authorities — what was it called?
Republic of Rose Island: 1968 micronation in the Adriatic Sea. The Italian government viewed it as a ploy by Rosa to raise money from tourists while avoiding national taxation.
Born in Tampico, Illinois, this future actor started as a sports broadcaster in Iowa in 1933 before moving to Hollywood and later serving as Screen Actors Guild president twice. Who was he?
Ronald Reagan: President of the United States from 1981 to 1989.
Taken as a Mughal hostage at age nine to enforce his father's treaty, this man later ruled from 1681 to 1689 as the second king of a major Indian empire — who is he?
Sambhaji: Chhatrapati of the Marathas from 1681 to 1689.
Nicknamed "the Grim," this Ottoman sultan grew his empire by seventy percent in just eight years, conquering the entire Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt between 1516 and 1517 — who was he?
Selim I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1512 to 1520.
After a 1969 coup, this army commander became Somalia's third president and reconstituted the country as a one-party Marxist-Leninist state — who is he?
Siad Barre: President of Somalia from 1969 to 1991.

Traditionally blamed on Queen Catherine de' Medici, this 1572 wave of Catholic mob violence targeted Huguenots gathered in Paris for a royal wedding during the French Wars of Religion. By what name is it known?
St. Bartholomew's Day massacre: 1572 killing of Huguenots in France.
Nicknamed for both his towering height and his 23-year run, this architect of the 'Swedish Model' welfare state holds the record as his country's longest-serving prime minister — who was he?
Tage Erlander: Prime Minister of Sweden from 1946 to 1969.
Of African descent through his mother, this French Revolutionary Wars general was one of only a handful of men of color to command European troops as a general officer in that era — who is he?
This Mitsubishi engineer had the extraordinarily unlucky distinction of being caught in both the Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings in August 1945 — and lived to tell about it. Who is he?
Tsutomu Yamaguchi: Japanese atomic bombing survivor.
This French Romantic giant gave the world both 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame' and a sprawling 1862 novel that became a beloved musical — who was he?
Victor Hugo: French writer and politician (1802–1885)
Beginning in April 2014 with a Russian-backed uprising in eastern Ukraine, this conflict ended only when it was swallowed by the full-scale 2022 invasion — what was it called?
War in Donbas: 2014–2022 war between Ukraine and Russia.

A German Army intelligence officer in occupied Warsaw during WWII, this man is credited with saving several Polish Jews, including pianist Władysław Szpilman — his story was dramatized in The Pianist. Who was he?
Wilm Hosenfeld: German army officer (1895–1952) and Righteous among the Nations.
Having previously served as Japan's Foreign Minister and Chief Cabinet Secretary, which LDP politician became Minister for Internal Affairs and Communications in October 2025?
Which of these people was born first?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
John Ray (born 1627) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Toghon Temür is an astronomer. Toghon Temür acceded to the throne in 1333 after years of succession disputes following his father's death.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Euclid is a mathematician. Euclid (Ancient Greek: Εὐκλείδης; fl. 300 BC) was an ancient Greek mathematician active as a geometer and logician.
What is the atomic number of Antimony?
Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium) and atomic number 51.
What is the atomic number of Chromium?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
In what year was Dolph Lundgren born?
Dolph Lundgren: Hans "Dolph" Lundgren (Swedish: [ˈdɔlːf ˈlɵ̌nːdɡreːn]; born 3 November 1957) is a Swedish-American actor, filmmaker, and martial artist.
In what year was Peng Liyuan born?
Peng Liyuan: Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).
In what year was Euclid born?
Euclid: Euclid (Ancient Greek: Εὐκλείδης; fl. 300 BC) was an ancient Greek mathematician active as a geometer and logician.
In what year did Pope Benedict XVI die?
Pope Benedict XVI: Following his resignation, he chose to be known as "pope emeritus", a title he held until his death on 31 December 2022.
In what year did Mileva Marić die?
Mileva Marić: Marić and Einstein were study colleagues and lovers, and had a daughter Lieserl in 1902, who likely died of scarlet fever at one and a half years old.
In what year was Theobroma cacao discovered?
Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Mikoyan MiG-31: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-31 is the fastest known operational combat aircraft, with a top speed around 3,000 km/h (1,600 knots).
Which company manufactures CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Chengdu Aircraft Industry Group. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
In which country did the CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder take place?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: People's Republic of China. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Darmstadtium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Darmstadtium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Who is credited with discovering 2 Pallas?
2 Pallas: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers. Pallas (minor-planet designation: 2 Pallas) is the third-largest asteroid in the Solar System by volume and mass.
Who is credited with discovering Multiple sclerosis?
Multiple sclerosis: Jean-Martin Charcot. It is a type of demyelinating disease, where the nervous system's ability to transmit signals is damaged.
One of the very few semiaquatic vipers in the world, which venomous pit viper native to the southeastern United States is often found coiled near slow-moving lakes, streams, and marshes?
Agkistrodon piscivorus is a species of venomous snake, a pit viper in the subfamily Crotalinae of the family Viperidae.
This group of large, semiaquatic boas native to tropical South America includes the green species, among the largest snakes on Earth — name the group?
Anaconda are a group of large boas of the genus Eunectes.
Native to Europe but introduced to North America, this orb-weaver spider species is known by several common names, one of them shared confusingly with a different species — which species?
Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.

With the symbol Ba and atomic number 56, this soft, silvery alkaline earth metal is so reactive it's never found free in nature, and takes its name from a Greek word meaning 'heavy' — name this element?
Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
This colourless industrial compound, easily dissolved in organic solvents but not water, is the key ingredient in most polycarbonate plastics — which chemical?
Bisphenol A (BPA) is a chemical compound primarily used in the manufacturing of various plastics.
This cabbage-family vegetable, whose large dark-green flowering head is eaten as food, closely resembles its paler relative cauliflower — name it?
Domesticated roughly 6,000 years ago in Mexico, this nightshade produces berries in red, green, and yellow ranging from mild to fiery — what is its scientific name?
Capsicum annuum is a flowering plant in the family Solanaceae (nightshades), native to the northern regions of South America and to southwestern North America.
Its other name is varicella, it spreads through the air, and it tends to hit adults harder than children — which itchy, blister-forming disease is this?
Chickenpox is a highly contagious disease caused by varicella zoster virus (VZV), a member of the herpesvirus family.

Lacking the sucking mouthparts of aphids, this chewing-mouthed insect is considered one of the most primitive alive — and a famous few of its 4,600 species became notorious household pests. What is it?
Cockroach (or roaches) are insects belonging to the order Blattodea (Blattaria).
Which compound acts as a cellular buffer and, via its phosphorylated form, hands phosphate groups back to ADP to recharge ATP in muscle and brain?
Creatine (or) is an organic compound that, in vertebrates, facilitates recycling of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), primarily in muscle and brain tissue.
Defined as having at least three loose or watery bowel movements in a day, this common condition can quickly cause dehydration, especially in children. What condition is it?
Diarrhea (American English), also spelled diarrhoea (British English), is the condition of having at least three loose, liquid, or watery bowel movements in a day.

Dubbed 'the father of public relations' in his obituary, this Austrian-American pioneer orchestrated a famous 1929 campaign branding cigarettes as feminist 'Torches of Freedom' to encourage women to smoke — who was he?

Edward Bernays (bur-NAYZ; Austrian; November 22, 1891 March 9, 1995) was an Austrian-American pioneer in the field of public relations and propaganda, referred to in his obituary as "the father of public relations".
This antibiotic treats everything from respiratory infections to syphilis, and as an eye ointment is routinely dabbed on newborns to ward off infection — which drug is it?
Erythromycin (sometimes abbreviated ETM in reports) is an antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Which evergreen conifer genus has needle-like leaves attached singly to the branch by a circular base, and cones that stand upright like a cedar's rather than hanging down? What is it?
Fir are evergreen coniferous trees belonging to the genus Abies in the family Pinaceae.
Named for a long-nosed, insect-eating African animal, this retired supersonic fighter-bomber pioneered variable-sweep wings and automated terrain-following radar in the 1960s — which aircraft?
General Dynamics F-111 Aardvark is a retired, supersonic, medium-range fighter-bomber.
What common name covers a diverse family of marine ray-finned fish in the order Perciformes, most belonging to the genera Epinephelus or Mycteroperca?
Grouper are a diverse group of marine ray-finned fish in the family Epinephelidae, in the order Perciformes.
Named after the physicist who first proved the existence of electromagnetic waves, this SI unit measures one cycle per second. What unit is it?
Hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.
Triggered by causes like vomiting, diarrhea, or the diuretic furosemide, this condition denotes a blood potassium level under 3.5 mmol/L — what is it?
Hypokalemia is a low level of potassium (K+) in the blood serum.
Known for the mantra 'Dying is not a crime,' this euthanasia advocate served eight years in prison after his fourth trial ended in a murder conviction — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian (May 26, 1928 - June 3, 2011), also known by the nickname "Dr.
This 19th-century French mathematician ranged across number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics — and his name now sits on a crater on the Moon. Who was he?

Joseph Liouville (24 March 1809 - 8 September 1882) was a French mathematician who worked on a number of different fields in mathematics, including number theory, complex analysis, and mathematical physics.
This genus of deciduous conifers, unusual for shedding its needles each year, dominates the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada, making it the most abundant tree genus on Earth — what is it called?
Larch are deciduous conifers in the genus Larix, of the family Pinaceae.
Equal to one cubic decimetre, this metric unit of volume was originally a base unit of the French metric system and derives its name from an old French unit of weight. What unit is it?

Litre (Commonwealth spelling) or liter (American spelling) (SI symbols L and l, other symbol used:) is a metric unit of volume. It is equal to 1 cubic decimetre (dm3), 1000 cubic centimetres (cm3) or 0.001 cubic metres (m3).
With about 6,640 living species across 27 orders — rodents and bats leading the count — this class of vertebrates feeds its young on milk. What is it?
Mammal (from Latin mamma 'breast') is a vertebrate animal of the class Mammalia.
Together with the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, this monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe's fighter force throughout the Second World War. What aircraft is it?
Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Its English name passed from Greek to Latin to Portuguese before landing in English in the early 1600s — which family of roughly 200 marine fish species boasts 16 genera?
Moray eel are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.

This branch of medicine focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cancer, a disease first documented in Egypt as early as 3000 BCE in the Edwin Smith papyrus — what is this medical specialty called?
Oncology is a branch of medicine that deals with the study, treatment, diagnosis, and prevention of cancer.
Designed by Niklaus Wirth to encourage structured programming and named after a French mathematician-philosopher, this language was developed in the pattern of ALGOL 60 — name it?

Pascal (programming language) is an imperative and procedural programming language, designed by Niklaus Wirth as a small, efficient language intended to encourage good programming practices using structured programming and data structuring.

Left untreated, this inherited metabolic disorder — caused by a faulty gene needed to break down a certain amino acid — can cause intellectual disability, seizures, and a musty body odor — what is it?
Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
Revered as the 'Father of the Nation,' this Emirati statesman served as the founding president of a Gulf federation from its 1971 independence until his death in 2004. Who is he?
Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
Split into roughly a dozen Afrotropical species and around 167 Neotropical species — among them the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which bird family is this?
Psittacidae is one of three families of true parrots.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging between 6 and 18 months of age, this genetic disorder, caused mainly by mutations in the MECP2 gene, brings repetitive movements, slowed growth, and language impairment — which condition?
Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6-18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.
Named for the Latin word for willow tree, from which it was first derived, this plant hormone is both a precursor to aspirin and a common ingredient in anti-acne skincare — which compound?
Salicylic acid is an organic compound with the formula C7H6O3.
Domesticated well over 3,000 years ago and grown widely in India, Myanmar, and Sudan today, this plant is considered one of the oldest oilseed crops known to humanity — what is it?
Sesame (Sesamum indicum) is a plant in the genus Sesamum, also called benne.
Native to a swath from Ireland to southern China, this aromatic herb is used to flavor food and herbal teas, and its extracted oil serves as both a flavoring and a scent — what is it?

Spearmint (Mentha spicata), also known as garden mint, common mint, lamb mint and mackerel mint, is native to Europe and southern temperate Asia, extending from Ireland in the west to southern China in the east.
This Chinese physician and revolutionary led the 1911 Revolution, overthrew the Qing dynasty, and founded the Republic of China as its first president. Who was he?
Sun Yat-sen (12 November 1866 - 12 March 1925) was a Chinese physician, revolutionary and political philosopher who founded the Republic of China (ROC) and the Kuomintang (KMT).
A metabolite of caffeine processed in the liver, this bitter alkaloid is the main one in the cacao plant and turns up in chocolate, tea, and kola nuts. What is it?
Theobromine is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Caused by a single-celled parasite and often symptom-free, this common STI can be diagnosed by examining vaginal fluid under a microscope or with a DNA test — what is it?
Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.

Native to Europe and parts of Asia, this parasitic plant draws water and nutrients from host trees and has long featured in European mythology, now commonly used in Christmas decorations — what is it?
Viscum album is a species of mistletoe in the family Santalaceae, commonly called European mistletoe, common mistletoe, or simply mistletoe (Old English mistle).
Making up just 1% of described fungal species, these single-celled eukaryotes reproduce by budding or fission and usually measure a mere 3–4 micrometers across — what are they?
Yeast is any species of fungus that grows primarily in a unicellular form and reproduces via budding or fission.
Caused by excess growth hormone after the body's growth plates have closed, this disorder first shows up as enlarged hands and feet before affecting the jaw and forehead — what condition is it?
Acromegaly: Human disease that results in excess growth of certain parts of the body.
Also called the Persian silk tree or mimosa tree, this flowering species in the pea family is native to Asia — what is it?

Albizia julibrissin: Species of plant. Albizia julibrissin, the Persian silk tree, pink silk tree, or mimosa tree, is a species of tree in the Fabaceae family, native to southwestern and eastern Asia.
Despite being named after a European bird for its reddish-orange breast, this thrush is the most abundant landbird on its continent, numbering some 370 million individuals — what is it?
American robin: Species of bird. The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.
Belonging to the suborder Vermilingua and closely related to sloths, these mammals include giant, silky, and tamandua species that feed almost exclusively on ants and termites — what are they called?
Anteater: Mammals known for eating ants and termites.
Who is this — “German murderer and cannibal (born 1961)”?

Armin Meiwes: German murderer and cannibal (born 1961). After Meiwes and the victim jointly attempted to eat the victim's severed penis, Meiwes murdered his victim and proceeded to eat a large amount of his flesh.
Evolving from a troubled twin-engine predecessor into a four-engine heavy bomber powered by Rolls-Royce Merlin engines, which British WWII aircraft became one of the RAF's most famous bombers?
Avro Lancaster: World War II British heavy bomber aircraft.

When no one else had the staff for it, this American lawyer volunteered to prosecute the Einsatzgruppen trial at Nuremberg, then spent decades championing an International Criminal Court — who was he?
This small, fluid-filled pocket that forms in the skin's upper layers — usually from friction, burns, or infection — gets the name 'bleb' when it's especially tiny. What is it?
Blister: Small pocket of fluid within the upper layers of the skin. The word "blister" entered English in the 14th century.
Typically about two-thirds copper and one-third zinc, which prehistoric substitutional alloy differs from bronze, which swaps in tin instead of zinc?
Brass: Alloy of copper and zinc. Brass has long been popular for its bright, golden appearance and is used for drawer pulls and doorknobs.
This silvery-gold alkali metal has a melting point just above room temperature, making it one of only five elemental metals that go liquid in warm conditions — what is it?
Caesium: Chemical element with atomic number 55 (Cs)
This Cornell astronomer worked on the Mariner, Viking, and Voyager missions and won a Pulitzer for 'The Dragons of Eden' — who is this famed science communicator?
Carl Sagan: American scientist and science communicator (1934–1996)
Known commonly as tapeworms, this class of ribbon-like parasitic flatworms sheds egg-packed segments called proglottids — what is this class called?
Cestoda: Class of flatworms. Cestoda is a class of parasitic worms in the flatworm phylum (Platyhelminthes).
Known for an exceptionally loud song produced by rapid buckling of drum-like tymbals, some periodical members of this insect superfamily emerge en masse only every 13 or 17 years — which insect?
Cicada: Superfamily of insects. The cicadas are a superfamily, the Cicadoidea, of insects in the order Hemiptera (true bugs).
Also known as ubiquinone, this antioxidant cofactor helps mitochondria produce ATP and gets its name from ten isoprenyl units in its molecular tail — what is it?
Coenzyme Q10: Biochemical cofactor and antioxidant. Coenzyme Q (CoQ), also known as ubiquinone, is a naturally occurring biochemical cofactor (coenzyme) and an antioxidant produced by the human body.
A heart disease involving reduced blood flow to cardiac muscle due to buildup of plaque in heart arteries — the most common cardiovascular disease. What is it?
Coronary artery disease: Reduction of blood flow to the heart. Procedures such as percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass surgery (CABG) may be used in severe disease.
This closed sac in the body, distinct from an abscess of pus, forms a shell of abnormal cells and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — what is it, medically?
Cyst: Closed sac growth on the body. A cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.

Found in many cough and cold medicines, this morphinan-class compound was approved by the FDA in 2022 as part of a rapid-acting antidepressant combo, but can act as a dissociative hallucinogen at high doses. What substance is it?
Dextromethorphan: Cough suppressant and dissociative drug.
Sold over the counter as Unisom and combined with vitamin B6 to ease morning sickness, this first-generation antihistamine is one of the world's most widely used sleep aids — which drug?
Doxylamine: First-generation antihistamine used as a short-term sedative and hypnotic (sleep aid)
Appointed to the Supreme Court by Barack Obama in 2010, this former Harvard Law dean became the fourth woman ever to serve as a justice — who is she?
Elena Kagan: US Supreme Court justice since 2010.
A rod-shaped gut bacterium that's mostly harmless or even helpful — some strains produce vitamin K2 and fend off nastier microbes — what is its name?
Sold in Italian restaurants as branzino, this slow-growing ocean fish is the most important species farmed commercially in the Mediterranean — what fish is it?
European seabass: Species of fish. It is one of only six species in its family, Moronidae, collectively called the temperate basses.
This genus of over 200 stinging insect species, Solenopsis, includes 'ginger' and 'tropical' varieties named for their painful bite and reddish coloring — what are they commonly called?
Fire ant: Genus of red ants.
This cold-weather injury turns skin white or waxy-blue after tissue actually freezes, often preceded by a tingling, numb warning stage called frostnip — what is it?
Frostbite: Effect of low temperature on skin and other tissues.
Named from Greek words for 'old man' and 'healer,' this medical specialty focuses on preventing and treating disease in older adults with no fixed age cutoff — what is it called?
Geriatrics: Medical specialty that focuses on health care of elderly people.
Born from an accidental 18th-century cross between the sweet orange and the pomelo in Barbados, this citrus hybrid is nicknamed the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit: Citrus fruit. The grapefruit (Citrus × paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.
The best-known of these rodents is the golden or Syrian species, though dwarf varieties like Campbell's and the Roborovski are popular too — what small pet is this?
Named after the 19th-century physicist who proved electromagnetic waves exist, which SI unit measures one cycle per second?
Hertz: SI unit of frequency. The hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.
This condition involves a buildup of cerebrospinal fluid around the brain, causing headaches, vision problems, and in babies a rapidly enlarging head — what is it?
Hydrocephalus: Abnormal increase in cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles of the brain.
Powered by four Aviadvigatel turbofans and built in Voronezh, this Soviet-designed wide-body jet now serves mainly as the Russian president's aircraft — which airliner?
Ilyushin Il-96: Russian four-engined long-range wide-body jet airliner.
Resembling a mustelid despite being a wild cat, this Americas-native feline comes in gray or red color morphs and once roamed as far north as Texas — which species?
Jaguarundi: Species of felid. Its range extends from central Argentina in the south and much of South America east of the Andes, through Central America, and into northern Mexico.
He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987, then later urged people to uninstall the product bearing his name and twice ran for U.S. president — who was he?
John McAfee: British and American programmer and businessman (1945–2021)
With an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters and a record of 5.85 meters, this snake is the world's longest venomous species, endemic to Asia. What is it?
King cobra: Group of venomous snakes from Asia.
He fathered the Ford Mustang in the 1960s, then rescued Chrysler from collapse as its CEO in the 1980s — one of the rare executives to run two of Detroit's Big Three. Who?
Nicknamed for the Greek goddess of wisdom, this roughly 22-centimeter nocturnal bird was introduced to Britain in the late 1800s and to New Zealand's South Island soon after — which species?
Little owl: Species of owl. It was introduced into Britain at the end of the 19th century and into the South Island of New Zealand in the early 20th century.
Nicknamed the 'maker of modern Mysore,' this Indian civil engineer and statesman's birthday is now celebrated as Engineer's Day across India, Sri Lanka, and Tanzania — who is he?
M. Visvesvaraya: Indian civil engineer, administrator, and former prime minister of Mysore Kingdom.

Studying under Rutherford at the Cavendish Lab, this Adelaide-born physicist discovered the nuclei of helium-3 and tritium and helped achieve the first experimental nuclear fusion — who was this Australian humanitarian?
Long before chemists called it 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenethylamine, this psychedelic was drawn from peyote and San Pedro cacti for spiritual ceremonies — which naturally occurring compound is it?
Mescaline: Naturally occurring psychedelic compound. The practice of ingesting mescaline-containing cacti extracts dates back over 6,000 years.
With over 17,000 built and flown by more than 50 countries, this Soviet-designed twin-turbine machine is the most-produced helicopter in the world — what is it?
Mil Mi-8: Family of transport helicopters.
Its wings make an odd whistling sound on take-off, and one pair may raise up to six broods a year — which abundant North American gamebird?
Mourning dove: North American bird in the family Columbidae.
Descended from Southern Italy's traditional guard dogs and closely related to the Cane Corso, this large wrinkly Italian breed was recognized in 1949 — which dog breed?
Neapolitan Mastiff: Italian breed of dog. The Neapolitan Mastiff or Mastino Napoletano is an Italian breed of large dog of mastiff type.

Flown by William J. Knight to a record 4,520 mph in 1967 — a mark that still stands — this rocket-powered aircraft was part of an experimental series operated by the Air Force and NASA — which aircraft?
North American X-15: Rocket-powered aircraft and spaceplane operated by the US Air Force and NASA.
The most arboreal of the great apes, with long arms, short legs and reddish-brown hair, this genus Pongo primate survives today only in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra — what is it?
Orangutan: Genus of Asian apes. The most arboreal of the great apes, orangutans spend most of their time in trees.
Commonly known as the bullet ant for its notoriously painful sting, which insect species inhabits the humid lowland rainforests of Central and South America?
This serous membrane lines the abdominal cavity and serves as a conduit for the blood vessels and nerves of the organs it covers — what is it called?
Peritoneum: Membrane that forms lining of abdominal cavity or coelom.
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie: French physicist and chemist (1859–1906)
Also called quaking aspen for the way its leaves flutter in the slightest breeze, which poplar species is native to the Old World's cool temperate regions?
This evergreen shrub or small tree native to South America is pollinated chiefly by the honey bee and gives us a popular tropical fruit — what species is it?
Psidium guajava: Species of flowering plant.
Born from refraction, internal reflection, and dispersion of light in water droplets, this arc always appears in the patch of sky directly opposite the sun — what is it?
Made of a large and small subunit built from RNA and protein, which cellular structure translates messenger RNA into chains of amino acids?
Ribosome: Macromolecular machine that synthesizes proteins in cells.

Built by a Swedish manufacturer, this single-engine fighter was the first mass-produced canard-design aircraft and the first with a digital avionics computer, unsurpassed until the Tornado arrived in 1981 — which jet?
Saab 37 Viggen: 1967 Swedish fighter aircraft family.
Native to cold-temperate Eurasia, this spiny deciduous shrub yields a fruit and oil prized in both cooking and cosmetics — what plant is it?
Sea buckthorn: Species of flowering plant in the family Elaeagnaceae.
Sitting just below carbon in group 14 of the periodic table, this blue-grey, brittle semiconductor is essential to plants and dominates the world's transistors and solar cells — which element is it?
Silicon: Chemical element with atomic number 14 (Si)
Commonly grown as an easy-care houseplant that tolerates low light, this genus of about 60 tropical species is better known by the nickname 'peace lily' — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum: Genus of plants. Certain species of Spathiphyllum are commonly known as spath or peace lilies.
Usually found in pairs and recognized as a leading cause of pneumonia since the late 19th century, which bacterium often lives harmlessly in the respiratory tracts of healthy carriers?
Streptococcus pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Streptococcus pneumoniae, or pneumococcus, is a Gram-positive, spherical bacteria, alpha-hemolytic member of the genus Streptococcus.
This orange citrus fruit is usually considered a mandarin variety, though it's also thought to carry some pomelo ancestry — which fruit?

Born from 19th-century efforts to make steam engines more efficient — thanks largely to French physicist Sadi Carnot — this branch of physics is governed by four fundamental laws relating heat, work, and energy. What is it?
